candidates.summary: the /docs default alias 404s on gno.land once this merges, and no in-repo test can catch it
candidates.failure_scenario: DefaultAliases maps "/docs" -> "/u/docs" (gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/app.go:30), and the diff leaves that entry alone. On gnoland-1 none of the gate's three rules holds for "docs": `gnokey query vm/qpaths --data "@docs" --remote https://rpc.gno.land:443` returns empty data, and `gnokey query vm/qeval --data 'gno.land/r/sys/users.ResolveName("docs")'` returns "(nil *gno.land/r/sys/users.UserData)\n(false bool)" (both run 2026-09-19). So every visitor and every crawler following https://gno.land/docs gets 404 "user not found" the moment this ships. The in-repo node loads examples/, which ship gno.land/r/docs/*, so rule 2 keeps /docs at 200 under TestRoutes: the one regression the PR body names is structurally invisible to CI, and nothing in app_test.go pins /docs either way.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb -run TestClaimsDocsAliasBecomes404 with the artifact dropped into gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ (expect PASS = 404), plus the two gnokey queries above against rpc.gno.land
candidates.evidence: live: `vm/qpaths @docs` -> "height: 0\ndata: " (empty); `vm/qeval ResolveName("docs")` -> "(nil *gno.land/r/sys/users.UserData)\n(false bool)". head test node: probe of /docs -> status=200 (examples ship r/docs). repro at head: "--- PASS: TestClaimsDocsAliasBecomes404 (0.00s)" with rr.Code == 404 and body containing "user not found".

candidates.summary: the shape check reads gnolang's Re_name, not the registry's own regex, so "not a copy that could drift" does not hold
candidates.failure_scenario: examples/gno.land/r/sys/users/store.gno:27 carries its own literal `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([_-][a-z0-9]+)*$` and its own `maxNameLen = 64` at line 30; it does not import gnolang. gnoweb reads gnovm/pkg/gnolang.Re_name plus a hardcoded `maxUsernameLen = 64`. The two agree today, character for character. The day the registry relaxes its literal (a third separator, a longer cap) gnoweb 404s a name the chain has begun to accept, and the 404 is silent because the shape check runs before any query -- the exact drift the comment says this arrangement prevents. The copy lives on the chain side, which the comment does not say.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'reName\|maxNameLen' examples/gno.land/r/sys/users/store.gno and grep -n 'Re_name' gnovm/pkg/gnolang/mempackage.go: confirm the registry holds a literal regexp.MustCompile and never references Re_name
candidates.evidence: store.gno:27 `reName = regexp.MustCompile("^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([_-][a-z0-9]+)*$")`, store.gno:30 `const maxNameLen = 64`; mempackage.go:70 `Re_name = r.G(r.C("a-z"), r.S(r.C("a-z0-9")), r.S(r.C("_-"), r.P(r.C("a-z0-9"))))`. Two sources, identical output today.

candidates.summary: every unknown /u/<name> now builds a GnoVM machine where it used to miss on qrender
candidates.failure_scenario: vm/qeval runs through withQueryEvalMachine (gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:1871), which loads the package, builds a gno.Machine and evaluates ResolveName for every shape-valid name with no packages. The qrender the PR removes from that path returned InvalidPkgPathError before building anything. /u/ is unauthenticated and crawler-reachable, so a walk over /u/aaa../u/zzz turns each 404 into a metered eval on r/sys/users. maxGasQuery and the rpcSlots semaphore bound it, which is why this is a tradeoff and not a defect; the PR body names the per-request cost ("the qeval is the heavier of the two shapes") but not the fan-out a 404 path invites.

candidates.evidence: keeper.go:1879 `pv := gnostore.GetPackage(pkgPath, false)` then NewMachineWithOptions at 1905; the gate calls userExists only when len(contribs) == 0, which is every unknown name.
